scoring_notice: Scores are analyst judgments using venturelab/opportunities.py weights, not probabilities, investment advice, or proof of willingness to pay. Eligibility checks only for evidence kinds; it does not verify source truth, quality, freshness, or commercial validation.

undated_sources.finding: Official Agents SDK docs describe native tool approval, pause/resume, durable run state and server-side security responsibilities. Current page has no asserted publication date. This is an approval primitive and a commoditization warning, not evidence of an exact-version client-brief approval product.

Current BILL pricing page lists AR invoice tracking, reminders and accounting sync in paid plans at $49, $65 and $89/user/month; not a price or willingness-to-pay signal for a separate exception queue. No publication date asserted.

Current Rocket Money feature page offers recurring subscription identification and cancellation assistance; it states more than 5 million cancellations. Current competitor information only; no publication date asserted.

opportunities.title: Invoice reconciliation and approved follow-up queue
opportunities.buyer: Owner or bookkeeper at a small U.S. B2B agency or consultancy
opportunities.problem: Overdue balances and mismatched payments require manual investigation and accurate follow-up before collections.

evidence.finding: QuickBooks 2026 report says 59% of surveyed small businesses had invoices 30+ days overdue (up from 47%); businesses with unpaid invoices averaged $17.7K owed. The source combines its ongoing survey (~5,000 quarterly respondents) and a Dec 2025 online survey of 1,305 U.S. owners. Strong problem evidence, not product purchase intent.

The report links faster follow-up and more automated processes with fewer overdue invoices, but does not test a new product. A standalone exception workflow would need reliable reconciliation across payment/credit/dispute data; current source does not establish implementation feasibility.

The report says 26% identify digital tools for chasing/collecting as useful. Existing accounting/AR suites already cover reminders and invoice status, so that signal is not unmet demand for another tool.

opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: Do not start a build yet. If existing ReviewGate interviews are extended to test this alternative, require a named budget owner, recurring exception examples and at least two paid pilots before committing engineering effort.
opportunities.kill_criterion: Reject if buyers already resolve exceptions adequately in their accounting/AR tools, no repeat manual exception burden is demonstrated, or no buyer funds a pilot.
opportunities.competition_risk: BILL and accounting platforms already bundle AR tracking, reminders, payments and reconciliation integrations; a narrow add-on would face data access and trust barriers.
opportunities.geography_limit: Evidence is U.S.-focused; India remains unvalidated. Survey-reported late-payment pain is not willingness to pay for this product.

opportunities.title: Human-reviewed AI client briefs for small professional-services firms
opportunities.buyer: Operations lead or managing partner at a 5–50-person U.S. bookkeeping or advisory firm
opportunities.problem: AI-assisted client drafts may be inaccurate or expose information, and teams may lack a clear record that a reviewer approved the exact version sent.

evidence.finding: Survey of 1,256 Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses participants, fielded Jan 27–Feb 4, 2026 across all U.S. states, DC and Puerto Rico: 76% use AI, 50% of users cite privacy/security concerns, 49% technical-expertise gaps; only 14% fully integrate AI into core operations. This cohort may not represent all SMBs; these are implementation signals, not software budgets.
Retained GAO engineering-risk evidence: inaccurate AI outputs and privacy/security risks support the need to control review risk, but are not firm-specific buying evidence.
The survey reports a need for implementation support but no specific need for standalone approval records. Provider-native approval APIs and bundled workflow tools may satisfy the underlying job.

opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: Continue only the existing narrow hypothesis: exact-version reviewer approval for one client-brief workflow. Keep the gate at 10–15 buyer interviews and at least two paid pilots before adding integrations or expanding scope.
opportunities.kill_criterion: Stop or change niche if interviews show no recurring review pain, no budget owner, or current bundled tools adequately solve it; do not infer demand from AI adoption or risk concerns.
opportunities.competition_risk: OpenAI Agents SDK already provides native approval and durable run-state primitives (see undated observation); basic approval logging is copyable. No moat or defensibility is established.
opportunities.geography_limit: Evidence covers a selected U.S. SMB cohort and general U.S. risks, not Indian demand. India remains unvalidated.

opportunities.title: Consumer unused-subscription detector
opportunities.buyer: U.S. consumer who pays for multiple recurring subscriptions
opportunities.problem: Consumers may keep paying for subscriptions they no longer use or want.

evidence.finding: CNET/YouGov online survey of 2,522 U.S. adults, fielded Apr 29–May 1, 2026 and weighted to U.S. adults: respondents estimated $21/month ($252/year) in unused subscriptions, versus $17/month in 2025. Self-reported consumer loss, not purchase intent for a detector.

The survey does not assess transaction-access coverage, classification accuracy, cancellation success, or consumer data-sharing willingness. A reliable detector requires these to convert reported waste into realized savings.

The report gives ways to find and cancel subscriptions; it does not establish a gap in existing money apps. Rocket Money currently advertises subscription detection and cancellation assistance (see undated competitor observation).

opportunities.competition_risk: Existing money apps already detect recurring charges and offer cancellation. Data access, trust and distribution are difficult; one-time savings may not support recurring consumer payment.
opportunities.commercial_hypothesis: Do not build absent credible evidence consumers will pay for incremental, verified net savings beyond existing banking and subscription-management tools.
opportunities.geography_limit: U.S. consumer survey only; no India validation.
